Issues.Title: fix(zone.js): keep the Node.js async context in microtasks
Issues.Body:
Previously, `then()` recorded only `Zone.current`, and every promise reaction in the process is drained from one shared microtask. Each reaction, the task hooks around it and the reporting of its errors ran in the async context of whatever scheduled that microtask, so on the server `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` could return the store of another request. Since `NgZone` runs change detection from those hooks, a whole tick could run as the wrong request.

Capture the async context when the callback is registered and run the task inside it, as Node.js recommends for custom thenables. Set `__Zone_disable_asyncContext` to opt out.

Fixes #71825
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(zone.js): keep the Node.js async context in microtasks" (#71826)

Issues.Title: zone.js: Promise reactions cause cross request `AsyncLocalStorage` context leakage in SSR
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

zone.js

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


With zone.js loaded on the server, `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` can return the store of a different SSR request.

zone.js replaces the global `Promise`. In `then()` it saves `Zone.current`, but not Node's async context promise

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/zone.js-0.16.3/packages/zone.js/lib/common/promise.ts#L545-L550
```ts
const zone = Zone.current;
if ((this as any)[symbolState] == UNRESOLVED) {
  (<any[]>(this as any)[symbolValue]).push(zone, chainPromise, onFulfilled, onRejected);
} else {
  scheduleResolveOrReject(this, zone, chainPromise as any, onFulfilled, onRejected);
}
```

The reactions then go into one queue for the whole process, and the queue is drained from a single native microtask, scheduled by whatever queued first ([zone-impl.ts#L1513-L1565](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/zone.js-0.16.3/packages/zone.js/lib/zone-impl.ts#L1513-L1565)):

```ts
if (shouldDrainWithNative || shouldDrainWithoutNative) {
  nativeScheduleMicroTask(drainMicroTaskQueueSynchronously);
}
if (task) {
  _microTaskQueue.push(task);
}
```

Node runs that microtask in the async context of the code that scheduled it. So when two requests have reactions in the same drain, all of them run with the first request's store. `Zone.current` is still right for each task, and `inject(REQUEST)` was right in every render I measured. What's wrong is Node's async context, which is what `AsyncLocalStorage` reads.

A lot of server code finds the current request that way: express-http-context, a pino logger with a request context, OpenTelemetry's context manager, Sentry. In my test app an interceptor forwards the user's token from express-http-context, and 20 concurrent renders called the backend with the same user's token.

Code in the app always goes through `then()`, because with zone.js in `polyfills` the CLI compiles `async`/`await` to generators over the global `Promise`. In both apps below, the zone.js server bundle has no native `await` left, while the zoneless build of the same source keeps 70 (Angular 22) and 80 (Angular 21).

```text
node v24.16.0, zone.js 0.16.3

test                          request   Zone.current   als.getStore()  verdict
A same-turn .then()           victim    req-victim     victim          ok
A same-turn .then()           attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
B shared in-flight promise    victim    req-victim     victim          ok
B shared in-flight promise    attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
C still wrong 3 hops later    victim    req-victim     victim          ok
C still wrong 3 hops later    attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
D native await                victim    <root>         victim          ok
D native await                attacker  <root>         attacker        ok

AsyncLocalStorage store from another request: 3/8
Zone.current from another request:            0/8 (2 are <root> after native await)
```

With 0.16.3 it's the same on Node 20.19.5, 22.23.4, 24.16.0 and 26.13.0,


Two renders have to be waiting on the same pending work. 

| | what both renders wait on | what the app needs | first requests of a process | after warm-up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the SSR manifest's `import()` of `main.server.mjs` and the index HTML | nothing | yes | no |
| 2 | the router's `loadComponent` | a lazy route that reads the identity | yes | no |
| 3 | the chunk of a `@defer` block with a `hydrate` trigger | that block, with incremental hydration on | yes | no |
| 4 | every `import()`, once an async ESM loader hook is registered | `@sentry/node` on Node 22 | yes | yes |
| 5 | a request shared through a `useValue` provider | that provider | yes | yes |

In all five, the same app without zone.js is correct. The other pieces only decide when two renders end up in the same drain.

Angular 22.2.4, on the Node versions it supports. `/account`, 20 concurrent renders with their own session cookie, first requests of a new process. Distinct bearer tokens the backend received:

| | Node 22.23.4 | 24.22.2 | 26.13.0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `@sentry/node` 11.10.0 with `--import`, no cache (4) | 1 | 20 | 20 |
| `useValue` cache (5) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| neither | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| zoneless, with Sentry or with the cache | 20 | 20 | 20 |

The Sentry row has no cache and no shared state in the app, and it gives the same result with the manifest's imports loaded before the server starts listening. On Linux with Node 22.22.3, which is Angular 22's minimum, it's also 1 token for 20 renders. It keeps happening after warm-up: over three runs on 22.23.4 the backend got 14 to 16 distinct tokens for 100 renders, and 84 to 86 log lines had the wrong user.

Sentry uses the synchronous `module.registerHooks()` only on Node 24.13+ and 25.1+ (`@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/cjs/register.js:28-34`). On older versions it registers two asynchronous `module.register()` hooks, and `@angular/ssr` imports the index HTML on every render (`ssr.mjs:1172`), so there is always an `import()` that two renders can wait on.

The cache in row 5 holds public settings and is shared on purpose: one `HttpClient` call, `shareReplay`, and `await firstValueFrom(...)` in each render. What crosses is the identity, not the cached value. After warm-up it was 69 tokens for 100 renders on 22.23.4 and 81 on 26.13.0.

The application doesn't have to use `AsyncLocalStorage` itself. I removed all the identity code and kept only OpenTelemetry's zero-code agent and the cache, and the backend received 1 trace id for 20 renders, on 22.23.4 and on 26.13.0. OpenTelemetry's context manager reads the store in `active()` (`AsyncLocalStorageContextManager.cjs:41`).

Cases 1 to 3 are inside Angular, and they need Node older than 22.18.0. Angular 21.2.26 on Node 22.17.1, 3 new processes with 20 concurrent requests each, renders that read another request's identity:

| route | zone.js | zoneless |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `/account`, identity read in a resolver (1) | 57/60 | 0/60 |
| `/profile`, lazy, identity read in the component (2) | 57/60 | 0/60 |
| `/` and `/settings`, `@defer (hydrate on …)` panel (3) | 30/33 | 0/33 |

Same numbers on 20.19.5 and 22.16.0. On `/account` without the cache, the backend received 1 distinct token for 20 renders and pino logged 19 of 20 lines under the wrong user. These three happen in the first requests of a process, after a deploy or a restart.

They stop at 22.18.0 because a new request arrives in an I/O callback, so it can only join an `import()` that is still pending after a turn of the event loop. One cold chunk import spans 11 to 18 turns on 22.17.1 and none on 22.18.0, the release with nodejs/node#57419 (*esm: syncify default path of `ModuleLoader.load`*). That covers Angular 21 on Node 20 and on Node 22 before 22.18.0.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/zone-als-leak

 ### Expected behavior

A reaction runs in the async context where `then()` was called, as it does with native promises, so each request's `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` returns its own store. Node's docs ask the same of a custom thenable implementation [async_context, Troubleshooting: Context loss](https://nodejs.org/api/async_context.html#troubleshooting-context-loss).

### Anything else?


It also works the other way around. If the attacker's request is the one that starts the shared fetch, the other renders in that burst run as the attacker: they load the attacker's account with the attacker's token, and whatever they write is recorded as the attacker.

This reminds me in part of [GHSA-68x2-mx4q-78m7](https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-68x2-mx4q-78m7), where concurrent SSR requests could also end up with another request's data. There it was the global platform injector; here it is Node's async context.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "zone.js: Promise reactions cause cross request `AsyncLocalStorage` context leakage in SSR" (#71825)

Issues.Title: Detect LCP images after soft navigations in NgOptimizedImage
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

common

### Description

`NgOptimizedImage` warns during development when an LCP image is not marked as `priority`. I think it would be useful to extend this diagnostic to soft navigations, so it also covers images displayed after navigating between routes without reloading the page.

e.g navigating from a product list to a product detail page can introduce a different LCP image. 
Developers should receive the same missing-`priority` warning when the browser identifies that image as the LCP of the soft navigation.


### Proposed solution

Extend `LCPImageObserver` to observe `soft-navigation` and `interaction-contentful-paint` entries when supported, associating them through `interactionId`.

Only paints associated with a detected soft navigation should trigger this diagnostic. An unrelated interaction that displays another large image should not be treated as a new navigation.

Keep the existing initial-page-load observation and use feature detection so browsers without these entry types continue to work as they do today.


### Alternatives considered

I previously opened #69963  if someone can take care of it or suggest an better alternative

References 

* [Soft Navigations and Interaction Contentful Paint](https://github.com/WICG/soft-navigations).
* [Measuring soft navigations](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/soft-navigations)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Detect LCP images after soft navigations in NgOptimizedImage" (#71812)

Assigning to a template reference in an event binding (`(click)="hello = bye"` with `#hello` on an element or `ng-template`) compiles without any diagnostic. The preprocessor's copy of the check is updated too, so both stay in parity.

Issues.Title: Custom property style bindings ignore static and `[style]` values of same name since 22.1
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler

### Is this a regression?

Yes, works in 22.0.8, broken in 22.2.4 and 22.3.0-next.3. Came with #68846

### Description

Hit this in my ui lib, had to move component inputs to separate variable

`[style.--x]` compiles to key `--%NS%x`, but static `style="--x: red"` and `[style]="'--x: red'"` keep `--x`. Styling priority looks values up by key, so these never mathc and binding stops seeing value of same name. `[style.color]` is not affected. No `provideCssVarNamespacing()` needed to hit this

- host binding `[style.--x]` now overwrites value author set on component element, before author won
- `undefined` no longer falls back to static or `[style]` value, element ends up without `--x`

| case | bound value | 22.0.8 | 22.2.4 | same case with `color`, 22.2.4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<my-cmp style="--x: red">` + host `[style.--x]` | `blue` | `--x: red` | `--x: blue` | `color: red` |
| `<my-cmp style="--x: red">` + host `[style.--x]` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |
| `<i style="--x: red" [style.--x]="v">` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |
| `<i [style]="'--x: red'" [style.--x]="v">` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |
| host `style: '--x: red'` + host `[style.--x]` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |

With `provideCssVarNamespacing('ns')` both stay on element: `--x: red; --ns_x: blue`

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

```ts
@Component({ selector: 'my-cmp', template: '', host: { '[style.--x]': 'v' } })
class MyCmp {
  @Input() v?: string;
}

@Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [MyCmp], template: `<my-cmp style="--x: red" v="blue" />` })
class App {}
```

`getAttribute('style')` on `my-cmp`: `--x: red` in 22.0.8, `--x: blue` in 22.2.4 and 22.3.0-next.3

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

None

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

@angular/core 22.0.8, 22.2.4 and 22.3.0-next.3, Chromium, JIT

### Anything else?

Compliance golden `style_bindings/css_custom_properties.js` shows same split: `--camel-case` in consts, `--%NS%camelCase` in `ɵɵstyleProp`

Issues.Title: fix(core): remove attribute when img/video attr.src is null or undefined
Issues.Body: The workaround introduced in #71095 converted `null` and `undefined` to `''` in `unwrapImgVideoSrcValue()`. While this coercion is needed for DOM property bindings (`[src]`) to prevent browsers from stringifying `undefined` to `"undefined"`, it inadvertently affected attribute bindings (`[attr.src]`). In the attribute binding path, coercing `null`/`undefined` to `''` causes `` to set `src=""` on the element rather than removing the attribute via `removeAttribute()`. Under standard HTML semantics, `` causes the browser to trigger an `(error)` event on the element, breaking existing usage that relies on omitting the `src` attribute until a URL is available. This change updates `unwrapImgVideoSrcValue` to accept an `isAttribute` flag and only coerces `null`/`undefined` to `''` for property bindings. Attribute bindings continue to unwrap bypassed safe values while preserving `null`/`undefined` so that `setElementAttribute()` removes the attribute.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(core): remove attribute when img/video attr.src is null or undefined" (#71799)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): exclude output directories from hybrid preprocessor tsconfig globs
Issues.Body:
When a tsconfig has no `exclude` (including through `extends`), TypeScript skips `outDir` and `declarationDir` while expanding `include` globs. ng-analyze didn't, so emitted `.d.ts` and `.js` files inside the project could get picked up as sources.

This only adds the output directories when `exclude` is absent, same as TypeScript. oxc already resolves both options relative to the config that sets them, so the comparison is a path prefix check. An explicit `exclude` is left alone.

Issues.Title: fix(core): guard hydrating map access and release pending task on error
Issues.Body:
`triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` accessed `blocksBeingHydrated.get(dehydratedBlockId)` with a non-null assertion `!.resolve()`. If the entry was cleaned up while the function was suspended awaiting resource loading or next render, this resulted in an unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'resolve')`.

Additionally, the pending task added by `pendingTasks.add()` was not guarded by a `try/finally`, causing the task to leak and permanently breaking application stability whenever hydration encountered an error or threw an exception.

This commit optional-chains `.resolve()` matching sibling accesses and wraps the queue processing loop in `try/finally` so `pendingTasks.remove(taskId)` is always invoked.

Fixes #71769

Issues.Body:
Starting in pnpm 11, `strictDepBuilds` is enabled by default and pnpm fails with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` when any dependency in the dependency graph declares lifecycle build scripts that are not listed in `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

Fixes #34622

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup
Issues.Body:
The karma builder schema documents the `poll` and `progress` options, but the application build it starts never receives them: `--no-progress` still logs build progress and `poll` does not switch the file watcher to polling. The legacy webpack-based karma builder honored both options.

Forward both values to the build options. No new test since both are pass-through options; the package unit tests cover the compilation of the changed setup.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup" (#34654)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`
Issues.Body:
In a Git worktree the development server keeps its Vite cache in the worktree's own cache directory while the configured path resolves to the shared cache of the main checkout. `ng cache clean` removes both since the `getCacheConfig` localPath addition, but `ng cache info` still reports only the shared path and its size, so the cache that the development server actually writes to in that checkout is invisible.

Print the local path and its size when it differs from the shared path. Outside of a worktree both paths are the same and the output is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`" (#34653)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): validate dist-tags and manifest caching under modern yarn
Issues.Body:
Modern yarn (`yarn npm info`) silently falls back to the `latest` version with exit code 0 not
only when a requested SemVer version or range is unmet, but also when a requested dist-tag does
not exist. Previously, `getRegistryManifest` only checked valid SemVer ranges, allowing unknown
dist-tags to resolve to `latest`.

Include `dist-tags` in modern yarn's requested `--fields` and add `parseYarnModernManifest` to
verify that non-range version specifiers exist in `dist-tags` and resolve to the returned
manifest version before stripping `dist-tags` from the result.

Move the SemVer range validation inside `#fetchAndParse`'s parser callback so rejected fallback
manifests are cached directly as `null` rather than storing the mismatched manifest object, and
scope `includePrerelease` to wildcard (`*`) specifiers so unmet major or x-ranges do not accept
prerelease `latest` fallbacks.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): use oxc-parser fallback when stripping source-map comments
Issues.Body:
Previously, `removeSourceMappingURL` relied on a custom character-by-character state machine to strip top-level `//# sourceMappingURL=` comments from JavaScript strings. Because that scanner did not track regular expression literals, quote characters or backticks inside a regex literal (such as `/"/`) inverted string boundaries for the remainder of the file. When a subsequent string literal contained `//# sourceMappingURL=`, the scanner misidentified it as a top-level comment and truncated valid JavaScript, or failed to strip the actual trailing comment at the end of the chunk.

Extend the single-trailing-comment fast path to string inputs and pass raw byte buffers directly from the Vite memory plugin so standard chunks slice trailing source-map comments without invoking a parser. When a file contains multiple or non-trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=` occurrences, lazily load `oxc-parser` and read only the `comments` of the parse result, avoiding JS-side AST deserialization while delegating full ECMAScript lexical handling (including regex literals, templates, and escapes) to Oxc. This keeps main-thread startup free of eager native or WASM parser loading. The fallback removes whitespace consistently with the fast path, removing comment-only lines entirely while preserving line terminators for comments that follow code. Also harden trailing URL and base64 validation so block comments or template literals closing on the same line are never misclassified by the fast path.

Closes #34590

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): enable oxc WASI fallback in WebContainer environments (22.2.x)
Issues.Body:
In WebContainer environments (such as StackBlitz and angular.dev playground), native Node.js addons cannot run, requiring oxc-parser to fall back to WebAssembly (WASI).

However, `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.156.0` specifies `@emnapi/core@2.0.0-alpha.6` while depending on `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime@~1.2.6` (which was updated for `@emnapi/core@>=2.0.0-beta.2`). In wasm-runtime 1.2.6, `initWorker` is assigned to `emnapi_shared.addonModule`, which is undefined in alpha.6 (where it was named `napiModule`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'initWorker')`.

This PR introduces `oxc-wasi-shim`, which aliases `addonModule` to `this.napiModule` on `Object.prototype` when running in WebContainer or when `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI` is enabled, allowing the WASI runtime to initialize successfully. In addition, `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` is removed from `optionalDependencies` since oxc-parser's built-in WebContainer fallback downloads and loads it on demand.

An end-to-end test verifying `ng serve` with `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=true` is also included.

Backport of #34628
Fixes #34524
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): enable oxc WASI fallback in WebContainer environments (22.2.x)" (#34629)

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): improve comparison-range colour in docs example
Issues.Body:
Fixes #31663

The comparison-range example uses `tertiary-container` as its background in M3, 
which is nearly identical to `primary-container` in several themes (e.g. Azure & Blue). 
The two overlapping campaign date ranges become visually indistinguishable.

**Fix:** Override two CSS custom properties scoped to the example host element with 
an amber tint — the same colour Material 2 used — so the visual distinction is clear 
in every M3 theme. No effect on user apps.

Issues.Title: fix(aria/accordion): avoid errors when destroyed before initialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34060.

`AccordionTrigger.ngOnDestroy()` reads the required `panel()` input even if the trigger is destroyed before the first change detection and `ngOnInit` has not run. Destroying a newly created TestBed fixture therefore throws NG0950, despite the template binding `[panel]` correctly.

Retain the panel associated during `ngOnInit` and only clear that association during destruction if initialization established it. Unregistering from the group remains safe for an unregistered trigger. This follows the registration/cleanup approach in https://github.com/angular/components/pull/33974 (combobox).

Adds an early-destruction regression test and an initialized control that verifies the panel association exists before destruction and is cleared afterward. The changes are based on main after https://github.com/angular/components/pull/34053.

Related Tree PR: https://github.com/angular/components/pull/34059. This PR is independent and contains only accordion changes.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the Chromium accordion suite reports **44 passed, 1 failed**; the new early-destruction test throws `NG0950: Input "panel" is required but no value is available yet.` The initialized control passes.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/aria/accordion --no-watch` passes: **45 specs, 0 failures**, including the strengthened initialized cleanup assertion.
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes.
- `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check` passes.
- TSLint passes for both changed TypeScript files.
- `git diff --check` and commit-message validation pass.

Tested with Node.js 22.23.4 and pnpm 12.16.1 on macOS arm64. The full Material/CDK/Aria test suites and Firefox were not run locally. Complete reproduction code, steps, environment, and actual error are in #34060.

Issues.Title: fix(material/select): prevent option selection while disabled
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #34044 with the corrected, fully styled reproduction. The earlier recording was missing structural styles; the video below uses the official theme and shows the parent Select becoming disabled before the option is clicked.

## Problem

I was playing around with `mat-select` and noticed a bug where:

1. Open an enabled Select.
2. Set `disabled` to `true` while its panel is open.
3. Click an option. The selected value changes and `selectionChange` fires.

Here is a reproduction video of the issue, recorded before the fix:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bd6a927-7f4c-4271-9227-0de589eb8b7c

This uses published Angular Material 21.2.14, the official Azure Blue prebuilt theme, and a standard `mat-form-field`. Click "Disable in 3 seconds", open the Select, and wait for the field to turn gray before clicking Orange. The readout shows that the parent is disabled before the selection. There are no forced clicks or custom select, option, or overlay styles.

The original recording was missing styles, which made the issue unclear. I agree that an individually disabled option already has `pointer-events: none`. This is a different state: the parent Select becomes disabled after opening, while its options are still enabled. In the corrected reproduction, an option has `aria-disabled="false"` and `pointer-events: auto`, even though its parent Select reports `aria-disabled="true"`.

A prop update can send `disabled=true` while someone is choosing an option, for example when an asynchronous request completes or a timer fires. I ran into this sequence while varying component props with Hegel and exercising UI actions with Bombadil in Anta, then reproduced the Angular Material behavior independently with Playwright.

My first thought was to close the panel, since that is what I observed with a native HTML `select` in Chromium. The [HTML option-picking algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#concept-select-pick) also stops without selecting an option when the select is disabled.

This PR takes the smaller step of rejecting user selection when the parent Select is disabled. It preserves the current panel behavior and still allows programmatic value changes. Closing the panel when disabled is a reasonable choice too, and I'm happy to adjust the PR to follow Angular Material's preferred pattern. The behavior I'm trying to guarantee is simply that a disabled Select stops accepting user selections.

## Validation

- The regression fails on the original source in Chromium and Firefox.
- `pnpm exec bazel test //src/material/select:unit_tests --test_output=errors`: Chromium and Firefox targets pass with the fix.
- Rechecked the styled browser reproduction: the enabled field turns gray, the parent reports disabled, and a normal click on Orange still changes the value and emits one `selectionChange` before the fix. No page errors.
- Current upstream `MatOption._selectViaInteraction()` still checks only the option's own disabled state.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/dialog): aria-hidden not restored when dialogs from parent and child are closed
Issues.Body:
When a `Dialog` is provided at the component level, it shares its list of open dialogs with the
parent `Dialog`, but each instance tracked the elements it hid with `aria-hidden` separately.
Opening a dialog from a child `Dialog` and then one from the parent (or vice versa) meant that the
instance closing the last dialog had nothing to restore, so `aria-hidden` stayed on the page
content after all dialogs were closed, leaving the app inaccessible to assistive technology.

This change shares the map of hidden elements with the parent `Dialog`, following the same
pattern already used for `openDialogs` and `afterAllClosed`. A unit test covering the
parent/child scenario was added; it fails without the fix.

Fixes #30028

This change dispatches a `change` event at the end of `setValue`, which is consistent with what
